findings.summary: The requested service root is a 404 error page, so its primary task cannot be completed.
findings.evidence: HAR records the main document as HTTP 404. The rendered page says the specified page does not exist and offers only a link to a different, insecure HTTP origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a useful service landing page at this public root, or issue a permanent redirect to the canonical HTTPS destination. Preserve a branded 404 only for genuinely missing paths.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the screenshot remains white and the computed body background is rgb(255,255,255); color-scheme remains normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and supply preference-driven surface, text, border, and browser-control colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The viewport blocks zoom and the only action has a 24px-high target.
findings.evidence: The viewport is maximum-scale=1.0,user-scalable=no. The page probe measures the dメニューTOP link at about 127×24px, below the common 44×44 CSS-pixel touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions, and enlarge the action’s clickable box to at least 44×44 CSS pixels without changing its visible text size.

findings.summary: A tiny error page has avoidable delivery latency and cache misses.
findings.evidence: Trace reports LCP 1.755s and load end 2.732s despite only 9.6KB transferred. HAR shows 1.421s for the document, three static assets without cache headers, a favicon redirect, and a parser-blocking stylesheet.
findings.suggestedFix: Return the correct document without the error/redirect chain, cache immutable static assets, inline the tiny critical error styles or ensure the stylesheet is promptly cacheable, and remove the duplicate favicon fetch.

findings.summary: The document has no main landmark.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reports header=1 and footer=1 but main=0; the error content is placed in an unlabelled section.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the primary error/recovery content in <main>; keep one descriptive h1 and expose recovery navigation with semantic structure.

findings.summary: The public root has generic, incomplete search metadata.
findings.evidence: The title is only エラー, meta description is absent, and the response is a 404. The page probe also finds no canonical URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a successful landing page with a unique descriptive Japanese title, concise meta description, and canonical HTTPS URL.

findings.summary: Indexing and navigation signals point to a broken or insecure destination.
findings.evidence: HAR records HTTP 404 for the root; there is no canonical URL, and the only crawlable link uses http://smt.docomo.ne.jp/. robots.txt and sitemap.xml could not be fetched by the raw client because the endpoint requires unsafe legacy TLS renegotiation.
findings.suggestedFix: Return 200 or a permanent HTTPS redirect, make all recovery links HTTPS, publish a consistent canonical URL, and serve robots/sitemap endpoints over current TLS.

findings.summary: The response omits baseline browser security policies.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive finds no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. The only recovery action downgrades to HTTP.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, CSP including frame-ancestors, nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; make every navigation HTTPS.

findings.summary: Styles are tied to physical directions rather than writing modes.
findings.evidence: The CSS/page probe detects physical left/right margins, padding, floats, and image positioning, and no logical inline/block properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace layout-relevant left/right properties with margin-inline, padding-inline, inset-inline, and logical alignment so the component survives other writing directions.
